paper.title_en: The impact and suppression of additional sidebands in atom interferometers: a review
paper.abstract_en: As a high-precision quantum sensor, the performance of Raman-type atom interferometers is directly influenced by the spectral purity of Raman beams. The electro-optic modulation method has become an important scheme for generating Raman beams due to its high efficiency and robustness against loss of lock. However, the additional sidebands generated during the modulation can cause issues such as spatially dependent Raman transitions, frequency-dependent carrier-to-sideband ratios, and additional phase shifts induced by additional sidebands. These effects degrade fringe contrast and induce systematic errors, thereby limiting the measurement accuracy. This work systematically reviews the generation mechanisms, influence mechanisms, suppression and evaluation methods, and applications of additional sidebands. It focuses on two main suppression techniques: optical single-sideband modulation and optical filtering. The review also covers research progress in theoretical modeling, parameter evaluation, and error compensation. Furthermore, innovative applications of this effect in atomic position detection and system calibration are discussed. Finally, this review prospects future development directions in this field.
